items.title: Richard Lloyd, Television’s Virtuoso Guitarist, Dead at 75
items.summary:
Richard Lloyd, who co-founded Television and played one half of the guitar partnership that defined the band's sound, died Saturday morning at his home in Chattanooga, Tennessee. He was 75. His family said in a statement to Rolling Stone that Lloyd died of cholangiocarcinoma, a bile duct cancer, with his wife Sheila and his dog Willie Mays beside him.

Lloyd was diagnosed in March 2026. A GoFundMe set up to cover his medical costs described tumors in his liver, including one lodged so close to a major blood vessel that his doctors could not operate.

Born in Pittsburgh on Oct. 25, 1951 and raised largely in New York, Lloyd started on drums and switched to guitar after what he called a hallucinatory experience. "My drums lost all their color — like in the Wizard of Oz in Kansas — and everything became grayscale," he wrote in his 2017 memoir, Everything Is Combustible. He played early on with Velvert Turner, a Jimi Hendrix student, dropped out of high school, and spent time in Boston playing with John Lee Hooker before returning to New York in 1973.

Television came together soon after, when the manager Terry Ork took Lloyd to see Tom Verlaine perform. "I saw Tom play and I thought, 'He's got it.' And I knew I had it," Lloyd told The Stranger in 2015. "But I was missing something and so was he." With Richard Hell on bass and Billy Ficca on drums — Hell later replaced by Blondie's Fred Smith — the band became a fixture at CBGB and Max's Kansas City, releasing the single "Little Johnny Jewel" in 1975 before signing to Elektra.

Marquee Moon followed in 1977, built on the interlocking lines Lloyd and Verlaine traded rather than the power chords most of their peers favored. Lloyd pushed to double-track his parts, stacking eight guitar tracks on "Guiding Light." As he wrote, "I did my very best to make it a record — not a live document."

The album sold poorly, and an opening slot on Peter Gabriel's tour did little to change that. Television split after 1978's Adventure, reuniting for a self-titled third album in 1992. Lloyd's 1979 solo record Alchemy drew good reviews and little business. Verlaine died in 2023.

items.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is A Box Office Hero With $32M Live-Action Foreign-Language Opening Record – Saturday AM Update
items.summary:
Gkids' Godzilla Minus Zero opened to $32 million domestically, setting a record for the distributor and the biggest opening ever recorded by a live-action foreign-language film in North America. The Takashi Yamazaki sequel took $14.5 million on Friday and earned an A CinemaScore, matching the grade given to 2023's Godzilla Minus One.

The composition of that gross is the unusual part. Deadline reported that Imax and premium large-format screens accounted for 74% of the weekend take, a higher share than Universal's The Odyssey managed with 52% of its $123.5 million debut. Gkids spent under $10 million marketing the film in North America and bought no television spots at all, according to iSpot. In Japan, the film has pulled $11.8 million since Tuesday.

Screen Engine/Rentrak's PostTrak put the definite recommend at 85% and overall positive at 95%. The West delivered a third of the domestic gross against 24.7% for the rest of the marketplace, and AMC Lincoln Center led all venues with just over $124,000 through Friday. Audience breakdown ran 37% Caucasian, 32% Hispanic and Latino, 13% Asian American and 13% Black. The overall foreign-language opening record still belongs to Sony and Crunchyroll's Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle at $70.6 million.

Below Godzilla, Warner Bros. Pictures Animation's The Cat in the Hat is tracking toward $20 million with an A CinemaScore, helped by a New Jersey teachers' conference that emptied schools and put nine of its top ten theaters in that state. Angel Studios' Drummer Boy takes third with $8.8 million, ahead of co-director Joel David Smallbone's 2024 film Unsung Hero, which opened to $7.7 million.

A24's You Can See Everything is estimated at $7.8 million in its fourth weekend, down 32%, pushing its cume to $78.7 million and past March of the Penguins' $77.4 million lifetime domestic total. Sony's release of Prime Focus Studios' Ramayana: Rise of a Legend lands fifth with a $7.3 million three-day, and Searchlight's wide bow of Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine at 1,100 theaters is estimated at $4.5 million, better than the $4.1 million start for his Seven Psychopaths in 2012.

items.title: James Bond Surprise: Robert Pattinson Screen Tested to Play 007
items.summary:
Robert Pattinson has screen tested for James Bond, The Hollywood Reporter reported, placing one of the most recognizable actors of his generation into a casting search that was widely assumed to be headed elsewhere. The 40-year-old joins Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor among those who have tested for 007. Nicholas Hoult has also surfaced as a candidate.

The tests took place the weekend of Oct. 24 in London. THR had previously reported that four and possibly five actors were in contention, though only three names were known at the time. Pattinson is currently shooting The Batman Part II in the city where the auditions were held.

The conventional read on the role had been that Amazon would avoid an actor already carrying a franchise, and Pattinson carries one of the largest — DC Studios' Batman. He also has a working relationship with Bond director Denis Villeneuve from Dune: Part 3, which opens Dec. 18 and is said to have gone well for both men.

This is the first Bond film made under Amazon's control after the company bought out the Broccoli family's creative rights in February 2025. Amy Pascal, who produced the Spider-Man films, and David Heyman, who produced the Harry Potter series, are producing. Pattinson's own career began in that world, with a role in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire before Twilight made him a global name.

The search arrives 21 years after Daniel Craig was announced as Bond in October 2005. Craig played the part five times, closing with 2021's No Time to Die, and his run included Skyfall, the only Bond film to pass $1 billion. Pattinson is also in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, co-leads A24's The Drama and anchors the studio's Primetime, and will receive the American Cinematheque Award.
